subject: Delegation request: limited subprocessor onboarding and TIA carve-out for SprintX pilot
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@springx.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@springx.com
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:43 -0700
Subject: Pilot onboarding: subprocessor delegation and temporary TIA carve-out request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — SprintX is ready to kick off a 6-week pilot with Redwood next week. Procurement asked me to send over the onboarding paperwork and surface one ask up front: because the pilot needs to provision a managed vector-store hosted by a third-party partner (VectorLane), SprintX is requesting a limited subprocessor delegation for the duration of the pilot and a narrow TIA/DTIA carve-out that covers only the vector-store operations for transient user IDs.

Attached: SprintX_onboarding_form.pdf and Procurement_PO_1234.pdf.

Key asks:
- Temporary subprocessor delegation (VectorLane) limited to pilot timeframe (6 weeks).
- TIA scope limited to pseudonymous vectors, retention < 30 days, no long-term identifiers.
- Confirmation on whether SCCs or UK IDTA would be required under Redwood's current routing for EU/UK data.

Can you loop in legal to confirm what evidence you need? We can be flexible on narrow compensating controls (e.g., contract annex, minimal encryption attestations) to expedite.

Best,
Anna Keller
Head of Product, SprintX
anna.keller@springx.com
+44 20 5555 1212

----

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@springx.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding: subprocessor delegation and temporary TIA carve-out request

Hi Anna — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Priyom (Product) so we can scope the minimal evidence set and the exact delegation language.

High level from ops/infra: we can support a time-boxed subprocessor delegation for VectorLane provided we have:
- Signed subprocessor addendum or a one-page annex specifying activities and retention limits.
- Confirmation of data categories (PII vs pseudonymous vectors) and example payloads.
- An assurance on egress controls and that VectorLane will not persist raw user identifiers beyond the 30-day window.

On cross-border controls: if the pilot will route EU personal data outside the EEA, we will need SCCs in place. For UK-origin data specifically, the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) may apply — that depends on residency of the subjects and the routing configuration. If the dataset is strictly pseudonymized vectors with no direct identifiers, we often can scope a TIA (DTIA) limited to that processing and rely on contractual annex + technical controls, but Legal will need to sign off.

I've attached a draft TIA scope (TIA_scope_draft.docx) that Priyom prepared with suggested fields for retention, access controls, and logging. Please review and confirm the data categories by EOD Monday so we can expedite.

Next steps:
1) Anna: confirm data categories and whether any UK-resident data will be included.
2) SprintX procurement: indicate acceptance of annex form or propose alternative language.
3) Kimberly: will advise on whether an amendment to the DPA or a short-term delegation schedule is required.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachment: TIA_scope_draft.docx

----

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Jun 2025 08:22:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding: subprocessor delegation and temporary TIA carve-out request

Markus / Team — thanks for flagging. I reviewed the draft TIA scope and the SprintX onboarding docs. Below is the minimal compliance checklist I need before Legal can sign off on a short-term delegation:  

Required evidence (minimal):
- Clear enumeration of data categories and example payloads (to confirm pseudonymization).
- VectorLane's technical controls: encryption-at-rest, role-based access controls, and a deletion/auto-expiry mechanism that enforces < 30 days retention.
- Proof of logging/audit capability for access to vectors (sample log extract acceptable).
- Contractual commitment from VectorLane: no retention of direct identifiers, subprocessors list, and obligation to notify within 48 hours of incidents.
- Confirmation whether any subjects are UK residents; if yes, we will require the UK IDTA addendum or a legal justification for an alternative (documented and approved by Legal).

Recommended contract approach:
- Short-term subprocessor schedule (annex) attached to Redwood's standard DPA, signed by SprintX and VectorLane.
- If SprintX cannot obtain the annex quickly, we can accept a signed letter from SprintX committing to the controls above and naming VectorLane as an approved subprocessor for the pilot only. Legal must still receive the technical attestations.

Risk note: temporary delegations increase operational risk if controls are not enforced. If VectorLane cannot provide deletion guarantees, we will not approve delegation.

Markus — please ask Priyom to get the sample payloads and a short statement from VectorLane on their deletion controls. I'll prepare a one-page annex (legal language) for quick signature.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Regards,
